M/s Patel Engineering Private Limited

Subject: Demand-cum-show-cause notice under Section 73(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 — Recovery of tax not paid / short paid for tax period October 2024 to September 2025.

Sir,

WHEREAS, on examination of Form GSTR-3B and GSTR-9 filed by you for FY 2024-25, and based on responses to ASMT-10 notice dated 18.07.2025, it has been observed that:

1. Excess Input Tax Credit of Rs. 8,42,500/- has been availed contrary to provisions of Section 16(2)(b) and Section 16(2)(c) of the CGST Act, 2017.

2. Of the total disputed ITC:
   - Rs. 5,20,000 — vendors not having filed GSTR-1 within prescribed time
   - Rs. 2,10,000 — payment to suppliers not made within 180 days as required under Section 16(2)(c)
   - Rs. 1,12,500 — invoices uploaded to GSTR-1 after the time limit under Section 16(4)

3. Applicable interest under Section 50(1): Rs. 1,51,650/-
4. Penalty proposed under Section 73(9): equivalent to 10% of tax demand or Rs. 10,000 whichever higher = Rs. 84,250/-

TOTAL DEMAND PROPOSED:
   - Tax:        Rs. 8,42,500
   - Interest:   Rs. 1,51,650
   - Penalty:    Rs.   84,250
   - ─────────────────────────
   - Total:      Rs. 10,78,400 (Ten lakh seventy-eight thousand four hundred only)

NOW THEREFORE, you are hereby required to show cause within 30 days from the date of receipt of this notice as to why the above amount should not be recovered from you along with applicable interest and penalty.

Reply to this notice shall be filed in Form GST DRC-06 on the common portal.

Personal hearing, if desired, may be requested through the same form.

In case no reply is received within the stipulated time, the matter shall be decided ex-parte based on records available.

(signed)
Deputy Commissioner of Commercial Taxes
LGSTO 23, Bangalore South
